title: Supreme Court Says Trump Can Deport People from Syria and Haiti
summary:
The Supreme Court made a big decision on Thursday. It said President Trump can end a program called Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for people from Syria and Haiti. TPS lets people from dangerous countries live and work in the U.S. legally. About 330,000 people from Haiti and 3,800 from Syria have this status.

The court voted 6 to 3. The conservative judges said the president has the power to end TPS without courts stopping him. This means these people could lose their jobs and be sent back to countries that are still dangerous. Many have American children who would be left behind.

Immigrant rights groups are very upset. They say TPS holders work in important jobs. For example, 15,000 are farm workers, 13,000 are nursing assistants, and 8,000 are caregivers. They also pay $1.5 billion in taxes each year. Ending TPS could hurt the economy.

The decision might also affect people from El Salvador, Lebanon, Sudan, and Ukraine later this year.
why_it_matters: This decision could affect many children whose parents might have to leave, showing how laws can change people's lives and communities right where you live.

background_read: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States; its nine justices have the final say on what the law means.
President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) wanted to end TPS for some countries.

TPS was created in 1990 to protect immigrants from places experiencing war or natural disasters, like Syria (where a long civil war has caused danger) and Haiti (which has faced many earthquakes and hurricanes).
Article_Structure: WHO: The Supreme Court and President Donald Trump.
WHAT: The Supreme Court ruled that the president can end Temporary Protected Status for people from Syria and Haiti.
WHERE: In the United States, affecting people from those countries who live in the U.S.
WHY: Conservative judges said the president has the power to decide without court interference; opponents worry about families and the economy.

perspectives.description: Believes the president should have strong control over immigration and enforce laws strictly.
